steps.text: Melt coconut oil in a deep pot over medium-high heat. Add onions and garlic; cook and stir until onions are translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in vegetable broth, curry powder, salt, coriander, and pepper flakes; cook and stir until mixture comes to a gentle boil, about 10 minutes. Cover the pot; boil for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Whisk in pumpkin and coconut milk until incorporated; cook for 5 minutes.

Fill blender halfway with soup. Cover and hold lid down with a potholder; pulse a few times before leaving on to blend. Pour into a pot. Repeat with remaining soup. Reheat briefly over medium heat before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Coconut Curry Pumpkin Soup
raw_recipe.description: This vegan pumpkin soup recipe includes curry powder and coriander and uses coconut oil instead of butter and light coconut milk in place of cream.

review.reviewBody: This was fantastic - a friend of ours made this soup for my husband and I a few months ago, and this recipe was almost as good as hers. I made the non-vegan version (used butter and chicken broth instead of coconut oil and veggie broth), and it ended up being very good. One difference between this soup and the one my friend made is that she added a little turmeric to hers, which I will try the next time I make the soup - it adds a little extra kick. I recommend topping the soup with flax seeds and pine nuts for a satisfying crunch! It's also nice to serve it with some kind of bread for soaking up every last delicious drop. Thanks for this great recipe!
I had to use the ingredients I had on hand. I only had chicken broth and Thai regular canned coconut milk. An immersion blender works great for blending the cooked vegetables and broth.

5 star for a baseline inspiration. I'm sure this is good as is but I made adjustments for my own thing... cook your spices with the onion creates a much deeper flavor so add them in the middle of cooking the onions before the broth. I added a bunch of cumin because I like that in everything curry, and lots of cinnamon. I added salt last which really enhanced all the other flavors. Used an immersion blender for a smooth and mustard seed speckled soup. I'm pretty sure I doubled the spices called for but that's personal preference. I had fresh pumpkin that was the inspiration for this, and I am pretty sure it was way better than using canned pumpkin. I also love making vegan and gluten free so everyone can have some!

Loved this but made incorporated a few changes: cut the oil down to just enough to saute the onions, doubled all spices, added 1 tsp cinnamon, added 1 tsp ginger, replaced the red pepper flakes w/ cayenne pepper (1/4 tsp), added 1/2 pkg of low-fat cream cheese (at the end, then blended with a hand blender to smooth it out). Wonderful, will definitely be making again!

4 stars as written. I followed the recipe almost exactly, except I did not use coconut oil, and I was doubling the recipe and ran out of vegetable stock so I had to use some chicken stock to round it out. We also found it to be kind of bland, so we added some cinnamon, ginger, and a little brown sugar, and that really added some depth to the flavor. I used full fat coconut milk and didn't think the flavor was overpowering. I did choose to blend the soup to make it a smooth texture, and I'm glad I did, though I think having an immersion blender would be a HUGE time saver here. A fairly healthy and (with the exception of the blending), fairly easy recipe. Served this at work for a pumpkin potluck, big hit!

I sauteed the onions in a light coating of avocado oil, reducing the fattiness in other reviews. I increased the spices to 1.5 times the amount called for and added cinnamon, ginger, and sage, which added a lot more flavor. Served in sourdough bread bowls, it made for a perfect fall meal!

Just made this for dinner and it came out perfect on all aspects; taste, texture, and color. I made some modifications though. Added a half spoon of turmeric to the spices, added the spices to the frying onion and garlic to release the taste and aroma, used chicken broth instead of vegetable broth, didn't have coconut oil so I used sesame oil instead (always like to use it in Asian recipes and carries anyway) and finally as I was using fresh pumpkin I chose to add it a bit early to the boiling broth to make sure it is cooked thoroughly. Overall amazing recipe and highly recommend it

I used 2 cut up pumpkins and boiled them down. Then I strained as much water out as I could. I quadrupled the recipe, used cumin instead of coriander, and then followed the the rest as written. I ended up with a gallon and a half of soup and the equivalent of 3 cans of pumpkin. So far it's a hit. I hope everyone at out Thanksgiving dinner thinks the same so I can unload on leftovers. I will definitely make this again.

We also like more texture, so omitted the blender step. In addition, I minced fresh ginger and sauteed it with the onion & garlic in unrefined organic coconut oil. NICE aroma! We had frozen our pumpkin from the fall, so used this and some fresh chicken broth with the coconut milk. (Yes, always dilute the coconut cream!) Added some cilantro & chives from our herb garden at the end, and voila! Perfect!

I used fresh, roasted, cubed pumpkin instead of canned, 1/4th the coconut milk called for because I only had full-fat Thai coconut milk available, and I added a tablespoon of maple syrup to give it a hint on sweetness, along with the exact amounts of the spices called for. It was very good, and we both liked it. My husband found it very spicy, but it seemed only moderately spicy to me… I suspect the leftovers will feel quite a bit spicier, as they often do.

I was curious about this recipe when I saw it, so I decided to make it today since it is cold and gloomy outside. Its a perfect day for a warm comforting soup. I followed the directions exactly, except for adding 1/2 tsp of cayenne pepper instead of flakes and adding a 1/4 tsp of ginger as well. I have never been a big fan of curry, but it is so good with the other flavors here. I love the layers of flavors. I also made cornbread to go with it. I would add, don't rush the 20 minutes of boiling the broth...it really melds the flavors and reduces the soup so it will not be runny. Thanks for the recipe, I will make it again.
Rather disappointing. Quite bland as written. Needs additional flavors and tang, and some sweetness. Good base.
Doubled the spices and served with toasted pumpkins seeds and sourdough bread! Delicious
I use frozen squash after cooking from my garden. It’s easy and a crowd pleaser! Our Favorite!!
We did it all in our Instant Pot. We used a fresh Butternut Squash instead of using a can Pumpkin. It's delicious! It's my new "go to."
It delicious. I made it
Great as is or with added carrots and granny smith apples... Also added extra coconut milk. Yum

Roasted my Jarrahdale pumpkin and used part of it to make this soup. I didn't have curry powder so I used Red curry paste. I also substituted graham masala for the coriander and used regular coconut milk. Everyone loved the soup.
Yes roasted with apples and red peppers. Omitted the nutmeg have allergy to it used ground cloves instead

It was really good! I added a dash more of each spice, plus garam masala, and cinnamon. Mine also needed a lot more salt. 
When I went to pour in my light coconut milk, I realized that I poured in only the cream, as it had separated, so don't forget to shake the can before you open it! Mine still tasted great, though. It wasn't noticeable.
